title: Velvet Anarkali for Winter Weddings: How to Choose, Style & Care
excerpt: Why velvet is the best fabric for winter weddings, how to pick the right velvet Anarkali, what to pair it with, and how to care for it.
body:
When the weather turns cold and the wedding invitations arrive, a velvet Anarkali is the one outfit that looks rich, keeps you warm and photographs beautifully. Here is everything you need to know to choose, style and care for one.

## Why velvet is perfect for winter weddings

- **It is warm.** Velvet has a dense, soft pile that holds heat – ideal for evening functions in December and January.
- **It glows in photos.** The natural sheen catches light, so colours look deep and rich in pictures.
- **It looks luxurious with very little work.** A simple lace or brocade trim is enough – no heavy embroidery needed.
- **It drapes well.** Good velvet falls in soft folds, so an Anarkali flare swings beautifully.

| Fabric | Warmth | Look | Best season |
|---|---|---|---|
| Velvet | High | Rich sheen, royal | Winter weddings, Diwali, Christmas |
| Georgette | Low | Light, flowy | Spring and summer events |
| Chiffon | Low | Soft, sheer | Day functions, warm weather |
| Silk | Medium | Shiny, structured | All year |

## How to choose the right velvet Anarkali

**Pick a jewel tone.** Wine, plum, emerald, wine, navy and black look the richest in velvet.

**Look at the trims.** Lace or gota on the neckline, cuffs and hem adds sparkle without weight.

**Check the lining.** A lined velvet kurta sits smoothly and feels soft on the skin.

**Think about the dupatta.** A light organza or net dupatta balances heavy velvet. A velvet dupatta can feel too heavy.

## How to style a velvet Anarkali

| Occasion | Jewellery | Footwear | Extra |
|---|---|---|---|
| Wedding reception | Kundan or polki set | Embellished heels | Potli bag |
| Sangeet | Oxidised jhumkas, rings | Clear block heels | Organza dupatta |
| Diwali puja | Gold jhumkas, bangles | Juttis | Bindi, gajra |
| Christmas / New Year party | Statement earrings | Pointed heels | Shawl or long coat |

**Keep warm in style:** drape a pashmina or a long wool coat over the top for outdoor functions.

## How to care for velvet

- Dry clean only.
- Never iron velvet flat – steam it from the inside instead.
- Hang it on a padded hanger or fold with tissue paper.
- Keep perfume and deodorant away from the fabric.

## Getting the right fit

## Frequently asked questions

**Is velvet good for a winter wedding?**
Yes. Velvet is one of the warmest and richest-looking fabrics, which makes it ideal for evening weddings in winter.

**Which colours look best in velvet?**
Jewel tones such as wine, purple, emerald, navy and black look the richest.

**Is a velvet Anarkali heavy to wear?**
A lined velvet Anarkali feels soft and warm, not stiff. A light organza dupatta keeps the overall look easy to carry.

**Can I wear a velvet suit to a day function?**
Yes, in winter. Choose lighter jewellery and juttis for a softer day look.
